structure.heading: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Execution and Customer Return Trend Implications
text_content: **Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Execution and Customer Return Trend Implications**

As of 2026-04-15, 9 of 12 CAPAs were closed, representing a 75% closure rate for actions issued in Q1 and early Q2. The CAPA register indicates three outstanding items remain active and prioritized for verification and monitoring. Closed CAPAs have completed implementation and initial effectiveness checks; doc.ation has been archived in the quality management system with completion dates and responsible owners recorded. Ongoing verification activities include sample inspection, process capability re-evaluation, and supplier follow-ups to ensure sustained corrective performance and reporting.

CAPA-026 (Vega—Connector plating thickness) has been open for 47 days as of 2026-04-15. The action addresses nonconforming plating thickness detected during incoming inspection and production sampling; root-cause analysis identified plating bath concentration variability and intermittent process control drift. Corrective tasks include tightened bath chemistry control, revised in-process measurement frequency, and supplier process audits. Risk assessment rates Vega connector function as moderate-high; expected closure depends on supplier corrective implementation and validation data, with a target completion window of an additional 14–21 days.

Customer returns for Vega increased from 1.1% in January 2026 to 1.8% in March 2026, signaling an upward trend that correlates with the plating thickness issues identified in CAPA-026. This rise elevates warranty exposure and customer dissatisfaction risk, prompting prioritized containment: enhanced lot-level traceability, expedited field failure analysis, and customer notifications. Preventive measures under consideration include process capability improvements, supplier corrective action verification, and quarterly trend reporting to accounts; metrics will be tracked monthly until a decline below 1.0% is demonstrated.

structure.heading: Q1 2026 Defect Performance by Product Line and Top Failure Modes
text_content: **Q1 2026 Defect Performance by Product Line and Top Failure Modes**

During March 2026 the production line achieved an overall first-pass yield (FPY) of 96.8%, reflecting incremental improvement versus February but short of the annual target of 98.5%. Product Line Orion recorded a March 2026 defect rate of 1.9%, maintaining the lowest defect incidence across core product lines, while Product Line Vega recorded 4.8% and remains the primary contributor to line-level variability. Monthly sampling and in-line test data indicate that higher variance on Vega is concentrated in mid-assembly operations and automated handling. These March metrics will be used as the baseline for April 2026 process audits and statistical process control tightening.

In Q1 2026 the single highest failure mode was Solder voids, accounting for 28.4% of all defects identified across manufacturing sites. Root-cause analysis attributes void formation primarily to inconsistent reflow profiles, insufficient flux activity on select solder pastes, and entrapped flux volatiles during wave and reflow operations. X-ray inspection trends show elevated void concentrations on larger thermal pads and multi-pin components, with a notable skew toward Vega assemblies in January and February. Analytical work included thermal profiling, paste lot correlation, and stencil inspection for aperture clogging. Recommended immediate diagnostics are expanded X-ray sampling, process window mapping, and supplier material review.
Cpk documentation for critical joins, and a two-week cadence of X-ray yield reporting to Manufacturing Leadership. Supplier engagement and retraining are scheduled.
